correctness.rationale: Lucas/Frobenius gives unit binomial coefficients modulo p. The unique k=q-r has r+k=q and valuation s-m; all other terms have denominators with p-order b<m, and v_p(k)>=min(b,s), giving valuations >=min(0,s-m+1)>s-m. A unique minimum forces valuation of sum and normalized residue congruence. The identity B*C(n,k)*r/(r+k)=C(n+r,r+k)*C(r+k-1,k) proves universal denominator divisibility, and valuation of B is m-s. Exact computations test boundary and multiple primes but are not the proof.

value.rationale: The binomial sum lies in the 2015-2023 nonintegrality literature. This result determines the full odd-p part of its reduced denominator and a nonzero leading p-adic digit on every prime-power-minus-one row for all shifts below that power, including arbitrarily large shifts beyond r=22 and small-shift regions of known asymptotic bounds. This is motivated by denominator saturation and Lucas structure, not an arbitrary numerical slice; the full denominator for general indices remains unresolved.
